spoilage_model.column_name_cleaning_rule: non-alphanumeric/underscore characters replaced with '_' (see reconstruct.py's _clean() regex)
spoilage_model.preprocessing_note: No standalone fitted preprocessing object (no sklearn ColumnTransformer/OneHotEncoder) exists in reconstruct.py -- encoding is done directly with pandas get_dummies(drop_first=True) on categorical_columns_one_hot_encoded, then the result is reindexed to encoded_feature_names_in_order with fill_value=0 (exactly how reconstruct.py aligns X_test to X_train's columns). There is nothing else to serialize for this step beyond the column list above -- a placeholder preprocessor.pkl would be fictitious and was deliberately NOT created.

rolling_features_required: roll_mean_7 (7-day rolling mean of total_demand, shifted 1 day)
roll_mean_28 (28-day rolling mean of total_demand, shifted 1 day)
demand_model.preprocessing_note: Same situation as the spoilage model: pandas get_dummies + reindex, no standalone fitted preprocessor exists or was fabricated.

risk_score_formula.nonzero_exposure_case: risk_score = 20 + 80 * percentile_rank(expected_waste_exposure among rows where it is nonzero)

item_category_lookup.purpose: Scales the demand model's category-level forecast down to an item-level rate: item_forecast_daily_demand = category_forecast_daily_demand * item_share_of_category. Computed from real TRAINING-period data only (no test-set leakage).
item_category_lookup.important_caveat: This lookup only has entries for items present in the original training period. It is NOT a general-purpose artifact for arbitrary future/company item_ids -- an item with no training history has no entry here, and item_share_of_category would be NaN for it. This is a real limitation of the frozen pipeline for company-data generalization, not an export defect.

category_forecast_lookup_NOTE: reconstruct.py also builds an in-memory (date, category) -> forecasted daily demand lookup (`cat_forecast_lookup`). This is DELIBERATELY NOT exported as a deployment artifact: it is a snapshot of the demand model's own predictions over the specific historical date range used in this run, not a reusable general inference artifact. For genuinely new (future or company) dates, the correct procedure is to engineer fresh demand features for those dates and call the reloaded demand_model.predict() directly -- never to look up historical predictions in this table.
